      "body": "SCOPE AMENDMENT TO I-0209 (the Z-clopen certificate principle) -- read together with I-0320.\n\nI-0209 remains mathematically CORRECT and is still a standing design constraint for anything\nthat needs a GLOBAL colength certificate: a DivisorAdaptation piece carries an R-finite-projective\ncolength iff its trace on Z is clopen in Z, and slicing Z along the base (basic-open refinement,\ndenominator-cleared pieces, Z-blind extraction) destroys finiteness over R. The k[u] counterexample\nstands. Do NOT try to repair a global certificate by localizing the PIECES.\n\nWHAT IS NO LONGER TRUE is the operational conclusion that this BLOCKS the DD-R lane. I-0209 was\nread for ~7 sessions as 'the certificate is unreachable, therefore DD-R is stuck'. The escape is\nnot a different piece decomposition but a different PREDICATE: localize the BASE, not the pieces.\nOver Localization.Away r the system is certified in the ordinary global sense for that ring, and\nIsLocallyCertified (DivisorFamilyZar.lean:71) -- which is all the consumers take -- is exactly a\nspan-top family of such base localizations. Base localization keeps Z finite over the new base;\npiece localization does not. That distinction is the whole content.\n\nLanded in run 0047: Picard/DivSchemeCertZarSeed.lean, DivSchemeCertZarPointwise.lean,\nDivSchemeCertZarTube.lean, DivSchemeCertZarKerSpan.lean, DivRepAffKitZar.lean.\n\nRULE: when a memory records an impossibility, check whether it rules out the GOAL or only one\nSPELLING of the goal. ---
name: horizon-waiting
description: How to wait for slow work (builds, subagents, monitors) inside a one-shot session — block in the foreground and get the result before you report; you are NEVER re-invoked on completion.
---

Your session is **one-shot and headless**. When you write your final report the
session ENDS and nothing calls you back. There is no notification when a
background job finishes, and any process you backgrounded is killed the moment
the session exits. So a plan like "kick off the build and wait to be notified"
silently fails: the notification never comes and the build dies with you.

Therefore, whenever a result you depend on is produced by a build, subagent,
monitor, or shell command:

- **Run it in the FOREGROUND and block on it.** Wait for it to finish and read
  its exit code / output within this session. A heavy `lake build` can take many
  minutes (sometimes 20+) — budget for that and wait it out; do not cut it short.
- If you must poll, **poll in a loop inside this session** until the work has
  definitively finished. Never end the session expecting to resume.
- Do **not** end with phrases like "monitoring stopped; it will notify me on
  completion", "still compiling, will report when done", or "I'll pick this up
  next session". There is no next invocation of *this* session.

If the work genuinely cannot finish in the time you have:

- Do NOT imply success or write a conclusion that assumes a pending result.
- Under `## Issues`, record exactly what is still running/unknown and why.
- Leave the explicit next action for a future run to pick up.

The one thing worse than a slow session is a session that reports a green result
it never actually observed. Get the result, or say clearly that you didn't.

---
name: lean-check
description: Build and check Lean in this workspace and read the errors — use Lean LSP MCP for fast proof-writing feedback, then run faithful kernel verification with `lake build` / `lake env lean`.
---

## Required proof loop

Load this skill before editing a Lean file. Before the first proof edit, invoke
at least one Lean LSP MCP query for the target (`lean_diagnostic_messages` or
`lean_goal`). After every proof edit, invoke diagnostics or the goal query again
before starting another tactic attempt. Use `lean_multi_attempt`, hover, and
search to investigate candidates instead of repeatedly launching a build.

Do not start iterative proof work with `lake build`: it is a slow, final-boundary
check. Use LSP for the edit loop and reserve `lake build` for the final session
validation (or when a kernel check is specifically needed). When LSP is
unavailable or crashes, record that in the report and use the narrowest fallback,
usually `lake env lean <file>` or a single module, rather than silently skipping
the check.

LSP is sufficient between edits and between separate obligations. Do not run a
module build after every proof or repeat a narrow build immediately before a
configured final build that covers the same files. At the final boundary, run
the configured build once and wait for it. Add an earlier narrow kernel check
only when LSP failed, the change crosses an interface LSP cannot validate, or a
specific elaboration/kernel question must be settled before continuing.

- During proof writing, prefer the Lean LSP MCP server for fast local feedback:
  inspect goals/diagnostics at the edited location before running a full build.
  This is the fastest loop for filling proofs.
- Treat LSP feedback as interactive guidance, not final verification. The
  faithful check is Lean's kernel via the project build: run the configured
  build command, `lake build <Module>`, or `lake env lean <file>` from the
  project root.
- Prefer the project's configured build command when validating a task. Otherwise
  use the narrowest faithful check that covers the changed file/module.
- Re-run after each change and repair failures you introduce.
- Read errors top-down — the first error often causes the cascade. For each,
  note the `file:line`, expected vs actual type, and remaining goal.
- A `sorry` left in place is an open obligation, not a success. Do not hide a
  hard obligation behind a new `sorry` unless a hint explicitly allows it.

## Fast LSP proving loop

The `lean-lsp` MCP server gives sub-second feedback — far faster than a build
(10–30s+). Drive proofs with it, then confirm with the kernel. Key tools:

- `lean_goal(file, line)` — the proof state at a line. Call before writing any
  tactic and after each one. Empty `goals_after` = that step closes the goal.
- `lean_diagnostic_messages(file)` — instant errors/warnings after every edit
  (`[]` = no errors, but *not* proof-complete — confirm with `lean_goal`).
- `lean_multi_attempt(file, line, snippets=[...])` — test 3–5 **single-line,
  indented** candidate tactics at once and see exactly which close the goal and
  why the others fail. The highest-leverage tool for filling a `sorry`.
- `lean_hover_info(file, line, col)` — type/signature/docs at an identifier
  (point at the first char). `lean_file_outline(file)` — declarations + line
  numbers without reading the whole file. `lean_run_code("#eval …")` — quick
  standalone `#check`/`#eval`/`#print`.

Core loop: `lean_goal` (what to prove) → search a premise (see the `leansearch`
skill: `lean_local_search` / `lean_leansearch`) → `lean_multi_attempt` (test
candidates) → edit with the winner → `lean_diagnostic_messages` (confirm) →
kernel-check the module at the end.

## Heavy builds — actually wait for them

Read the WHOLE build output, not just pass/fail: warnings (unused variables,
deprecations, `sorry` notices, unexpected recompiles) are actionable — fix the
ones your change introduced, and record pre-existing/toolchain ones as memory
or an inbox issue rather than scrolling past (see the `horizon` skill,
"Warnings are work").

A cold `lake build` (or one that recompiles Mathlib) can take many minutes. The
most common way a session ends on a wrong conclusion is **not waiting for the
build to finish**:

- Do **not** assume you will be "automatically notified" or "re-invoked" when a
  background build completes — whether that happens depends entirely on the
  mechanism you used. If unsure, run the build in the **foreground** and block on
  it until it exits, then read the exit code.
- If you run it in the background, you MUST actively wait: poll its status/output
  until there is a definitive exit code (a monitor / until-loop, re-reading the
  log), and only then conclude. A background job you started but walked away from
  is *not* done.
- Scope the build to the narrowest faithful check (`lake build <Module>` or
  `lake env lean <file>`) to keep the wait short; reserve the full project build
  for final validation.
- Never write your final report — or `complete` an inbox item, or mark a task
  done — while a build that affects your conclusion is still running. If the
  engine cannot wait long enough, say so explicitly under `## Issues` and leave
  the next action clear, rather than implying the proof checked.
- Before marking a task or roadmap item done/blocked/rejected, add a concise
  closing comment with the exact check command, result, relevant files, and any
  caveat. If a task has `roadmap_refs`, make sure the linked roadmap items end
  with a consistent status and their own sync/closing comment.

## When the LSP dies on big import files

The Lean LSP loads the full environment for the file you open. On a file whose
imports pull in most of Mathlib (a broad `import Mathlib` umbrella, or a module
that transitively imports one), that environment is huge and the LSP server can
run out of memory or time out and die. This is an LSP limitation, **not** a
proof error:

- Do not treat an LSP crash/timeout on such a file as a failure of your proof.
  Fall back to the kernel check: `lake build <Module>` or `lake env lean <file>`,
  which verifies faithfully without holding the whole environment interactively.
- Prefer opening the **narrowest** module in the LSP. Avoid pointing the LSP at
  umbrella/`import Mathlib`-style files just to get feedback; edit and inspect
  the specific module you are proving in instead.
- If the LSP has crashed, restart it (or just proceed with `lake build`) rather
  than repeatedly reopening the same giant file and getting the same crash.

---
name: project-git
description: How git works in an Archon Horizon workspace — one out-of-tree workspace ledger (no per-project repos); read a project's history by pathspec or by a session's commit trailers.
---

Read this before running `git diff`/`git log` on a project.

## The model

- **One out-of-tree workspace ledger.** Archon commits to a single repo whose git
  dir is `.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git` with the workspace **root** as its
  work tree (driven via `--git-dir`/`--work-tree`). `<root>/.git` is deliberately
  untouched — it is reserved for a user repo. The ledger records one commit per
  completed session: `config.yaml`, the session's scoped project files, and
  `.archon-horizon/` shared state; never the binary git dirs under
  `.archon-horizon/vcs/`, locks, or other volatile internals.
- **There are no per-project repositories.** A project directory has no nested
  `.git/`, and there is no `.archon-horizon/vcs/<project>.git`. A project's
  "history" is simply the workspace ledger filtered to that project's path.
- **You record your own work by committing to the ledger** with plain `git` (see
  below). Commit *early and often* with a semantic, math-first message — the
  commit message + diff is how your progress is read, so make the message say what
  you proved/built. Provenance trailers are added automatically; do not write them.

So a plain `git diff` at the root sees only a user repo (if any), never Archon's.
Drive the out-of-tree workspace ledger explicitly (or use `hgit`).

## Recording your work (committing)

Commits go to the ledger, **not** to `<root>/.git` and **not** via any project
`.git` (there is none). Do **not** `export GIT_DIR` / `GIT_WORK_TREE` yourself — that
would redirect `lake` and other tooling. Two equivalent ways to commit:

```bash
# 1) The `hgit` wrapper (on the session env as $HORIZON_GIT) — plain git, ledger-scoped:
"$HORIZON_GIT" add path/to/File.lean
"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "feat(chapter): prove foo_lemma" \
  --trailer 'Summary=**Proof.** Closed the compactness step using $K \subseteq X$.'

# 2) The explicit form (identical effect):
git --git-dir="$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree="$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" \
    add path/to/File.lean
git --git-dir="$HORIZON_LEDGER_GIT_DIR" --work-tree="$HORIZON_LEDGER_WORK_TREE" \
    commit -m "feat(chapter): prove foo_lemma" \
    --trailer 'Summary=**Proof.** Closed the compactness step using $K \subseteq X$.'
```

Ordinary git: the ledger's index tracks HEAD, so `add` then `commit` records your
files on top of it. Horizon's own commits stage in a private index and never leave
anything staged in your way.

- **Prefer the pathspec commit** — name the paths on the commit itself:
  `"$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "…" --trailer 'Summary=…' -- path/to/File.lean`
  It records exactly those files, ignores whatever else may be staged, and git
  builds its tree from the **current** HEAD — so it cannot silently revert a
  concurrent session's files the way a commit built on a stale index can.
- Add at least one **`Summary` trailer** explaining the important change, not
  merely repeating the subject. Use one trailer per distinct explanation when
  useful. Its value supports Markdown and LaTeX, so concise mathematical context
  such as `--trailer 'Summary=**Invariant.** Preserves $f(x)=x$ on $A$.'` renders
  directly in the dashboard commit item. Keep each trailer on one line; repeat
  `--trailer 'Summary=…'` for a few separate points.
- Stage **explicit paths** you changed rather than `add -A` — the work tree is the
  whole workspace, so `-A` can sweep in unrelated files.
- `Archon-Run`/`Session`/`Role`/`Task`/`Projects` trailers are stamped for you by a
  hook from the session env; your message stays clean.
- Build artifacts (`.lake`, `*.olean`, …) are excluded automatically, and any
  high-confidence credential is **redacted to `XXXX`** in the staged content (not
  blocked), so a broad add still won't leak a secret into the ledger.
- If the guard reports *"redacted possible secret(s) to XXXX"*, it scrubbed a
  matched credential and let the commit through — **rotate the real credential**,
  and check you didn't stage more than you meant to (`ARCHON_HORIZON_ALLOW_SECRETS=1`
  skips the scan entirely). A *separate* guard still **blocks** a commit that would
  silently delete tracked files you didn't change (a stale-index clobber); re-seed
  the index (`git read-tree HEAD && git add -- <your files>`) rather than forcing it.

Then verify **in the ledger**, and verify the **paths**, not just the SHA — a bare
`git cat-file` runs against `<root>/.git`, which has not seen your commit yet and will
make a perfectly real SHA look fabricated:

```bash
"$HORIZON_GIT" ls-tree --name-only HEAD -- path/to/File.lean   # empty ⇒ NOT in HEAD
```

## Concurrent sessions and the clobber guard

Several sessions may commit to the ledger at once. A commit whose index was
seeded from an older HEAD (e.g. `read-tree`, then a concurrent session commits,
then you commit) produces a tree that *lacks* the other session's new files —
plain git would commit it without any error and silently delete their work.
The ledger's `pre-commit` guard now rejects any commit that stages deletions
you did not ask for:

- *"this commit would DELETE N tracked file(s) you did not change"* — your
  index base is stale (or you are committing through a polluted shared index).
  **Do not override.** Re-seed and retry; your own edits are safe in the
  working tree, which concurrent commits never touch:

  ```bash
  "$HORIZON_GIT" read-tree HEAD
  "$HORIZON_GIT" add -- <your files>
  "$HORIZON_GIT" commit -m "…"          # or just: commit -m "…" -- <your files>
  ```

- Deleting a file **on purpose** (moved/retired): set
  `ARCHON_HORIZON_ALLOW_DELETIONS=1` for that one commit.

At the **end of the session**, re-verify content — not just that HEAD moved —
since a stale-based commit elsewhere could have landed after yours (the guard
blocks new offenders, but belt-and-braces):

```bash
"$HORIZON_GIT" cat-file -e HEAD:path/to/File.lean && \
"$HORIZON_GIT" show HEAD:path/to/File.lean | diff -q - path/to/File.lean
```

If you were clobbered anyway: `read-tree HEAD`, re-add your files from the
working tree, commit once.

## Reading history / a project's diff

Run from the workspace root:

```bash
GD=.archon-horizon/vcs/workspace.git

git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. log  --oneline -n 20                       # whole ledger
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. log  --oneline -n 20 -- <project-path>     # one project
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD~1 -- <project-path>
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. diff HEAD~1 -- '<project-path>/*.lean'
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. show <sha>
```

Each commit carries provenance trailers — `Archon-Run`, `Archon-Session`,
`Archon-Role`, `Archon-Task`, `Archon-Projects` — so you can map a commit to the
run/session that made it and see what it touched without parsing prose:

```bash
git --git-dir=$GD --work-tree=. \
  log --format='%H %(trailers:key=Archon-Session,valueonly)' -- <project-path>
```

To see what the previous Horizon agent changed, find its session's commit(s) by
the `Archon-Session` trailer and diff each against **its own parent** (what that
commit changed).

## Caveats

- With parallel runs the ledger is one shared branch: commits from several runs
  interleave, and a commit's parent may belong to another run or a dashboard
  publish. Diff a commit against its own parent (what *that* commit changed), not
  across a span of sessions — that would fold in unrelated runs' changes.
- The bundled author identity is `Archon Horizon <archon-horizon@local>`.

---
name: leansearch
description: Find existing lemmas/definitions before proving — the local `horizon search` index plus the Lean LSP MCP search tools (LeanSearch/Loogle/state-search/hammer-premise). Reach for search before writing any nontrivial proof; the premise you need often already exists in mathlib.
---

**Search before you prove.** Most facts you need already exist in mathlib or the
workspace. Searching is far cheaper than reproving. Use the local index first
(unlimited, instant), then the LSP search tools for broader semantic/type search.

## Local first: `horizon search`

An offline declaration search over `external_libraries` (mathlib by default) plus
the workspace's own projects. No GPU, API key, or network. Three modes share one
cached index:

- Natural language — what a lemma says:
  `horizon search "continuous function on a compact set attains its maximum"`
- `--name` — find a declaration by partial name:
  `horizon search --name isCompact.image`
- `--type` — find by shape of the statement; `?a`/`?b`/`_` are wildcards:
  `horizon search --type "Continuous ?f -> IsCompact ?s -> IsCompact (?f '' ?s)"`

Useful flags: `-n K`, `--lib NAME`, `--json`, `--reindex`. If results look thin,
run the project build so sources are current, then `horizon search --reindex`.

## Lean LSP MCP search tools

The `lean-lsp` MCP server (configured in `.mcp.json`) exposes a full search
arsenal. Rate limits are **per-tool** (separate pools), not a shared budget.

| Tool | Use it for | Limit |
|------|-----------|-------|
| `lean_local_search` | exact/partial declaration name; workspace + mathlib | unlimited |
| `lean_leansearch` | **semantic search by mathematical meaning** (PKU LeanSearch) | 10 / 30s |
| `lean_loogle` | search by **type shape** when you know the signature, not the name | remote; unlimited in `--loogle-local` |
| `lean_state_search` | lemmas that apply to a specific **proof state** (goal at a line) | 3 / 30s |
| `lean_hammer_premise` | **premise names** to feed `simp only [...]` / `aesop` / `grind` | 3 / 30s |
| `lean_leanfinder` | semantic fallback — only when `lean_leansearch` fails | 10 / 30s |

### Priority / escalation order

1. `lean_local_search("name")` — always first; unlimited, instant, deterministic.
2. `lean_leansearch("describe the math.")` — primary semantic search (see below).
3. `lean_loogle("?a -> ?b")` — simple type patterns only.
4. `lean_state_search(file, line, col)` — goal-conditioned lookup when stuck.
5. `lean_hammer_premise(file, line, col)` — premises for `simp`/`aesop`/`grind`.
6. `lean_leanfinder("description")` — last-resort semantic fallback.

### `lean_leansearch` — the PKU semantic tool (use it well)

LeanSearch (leansearch.net, from the PKU team) augments each mathlib theorem into
an informal description and matches your query against those embeddings —
returning the **nearest neighbours**, not just exact hits. That is its strength:
a theorem 90% of what you need is often enough; prove the small gap yourself.

- **Describe the mathematical content, not the name.** Query must end with `.`/`?`.
  - Good: `lean_leansearch("The image of a compact set under a continuous map is compact.")`
  - Good (mixed): `lean_leansearch("natural numbers. from: n < m, to: n + 1 < m + 1")`
  - Weak: `lean_leansearch("add_comm")` → use `lean_local_search` instead.
  - Weak: `lean_leansearch("∀ (a b : ℕ), a + b = b + a")` → use `lean_loogle` instead.
- **Trust a negative result.** If a precise, mathematically accurate description
  returns nothing relevant, the theorem likely isn't in mathlib — stop rephrasing
  and prove it (or find another route) rather than searching endlessly.

### `lean_loogle` — type-shape search

Searches by *type structure*, not names. Syntax: `?a`/`?b` type vars, `_`
wildcards, `->`/`→` arrows, `|- pattern` by conclusion.
- Good: `lean_loogle("(?a -> ?b) -> List ?a -> List ?b")` → `List.map`
- Anti-pattern: nested `Submodule`/`LinearMap`/`Finsupp`, 3+ typeclass
  constraints, or guessy implicit structure — use `lean_leansearch` for those.

## Discipline

- Treat every hit as a **candidate**: read the signature/source and confirm with
  the Lean checker (see the `lean-check` skill) before depending on it.
- Try multiple phrasings — project name, mathematical concept, conclusion/type.
- Local (`horizon search` / `lean_local_search`) is optimized for the checked-out
  sources here; the LSP tools reach broader mathlib precedent. Use both.

---
name: mathlib-conventions
description: Mathlib house style for the Lean you write — naming (snake_case props / UpperCamelCase types / lowerCamelCase defs, Is-prefix, le/lt), meaningful discoverable names, preferred abstractions, and how to add a missing lemma as reusable infrastructure instead of a local hack.
---

Write Lean that looks like it belongs in mathlib: discoverable, reusable, and
composing with the existing API. This is the style side; use [[leansearch]] to
*find* lemmas and [[lean-check]] to verify, and keep the blueprint in step via
[[blueprint-conventions]].

## Naming

- **Theorems / lemmas / `Prop`s → `snake_case`**, named by *what the statement
  says*, composing the pieces in order: `add_comm`, `mul_le_mul_left`,
  `isOpen_iUnion`, `continuous_id`. A reader should reconstruct the statement
  from the name.
- **Types, structures, classes, inductives → `UpperCamelCase`**: `LinearMap`,
  `IsLindelof`, `RiemannianMetric`.
- **Definitions / terms / functions → `lowerCamelCase`**: `leviCivita`,
  `koszulRHS`, `parallelTransport`.
- **Structural predicates take the `Is` prefix**: `IsOpen`, `IsCompact`,
  `IsSymmetric`.
- **Name order relations by the operator you wrote**, not its mirror: use `le`
  / `lt` (`le_of_lt`, `add_lt_add`), not `ge` / `gt`.
- **Meaningful names only.** No `helper1`, `foo_aux`, `my_lemma`, `lemma2`.
  Ad-hoc names are invisible to search and un-reusable — the whole point of a
  mathlib-style name is that the next session (or mathlib itself) can find it.

## Search before you prove, prefer before you build

- Your "obvious lemma" is very likely already in mathlib under a more general
  name. Search first ([[leansearch]]); a negative result after a precise query
  means it's genuinely absent — then prove it, don't keep rephrasing.
- **Choose the reusable abstraction**, so your work composes with mathlib rather
  than sitting in a private silo: `Filter`/`Tendsto` over hand-rolled ε–δ, the
  Bochner `MeasureTheory.integral` over an ad-hoc integral, bundled morphisms
  (`…Hom`) and typeclasses over unbundled functions-plus-hypotheses, unless the
  problem is genuinely about the lower-level object.

## Missing infrastructure → build it properly, don't defer or hack

When a needed fact truly isn't in mathlib, the failure mode is to leave a
`sorry` "waiting for an upstream PR", or to inline a brittle one-off. Instead:

- **State the missing lemma in mathlib-ready generality**, with a proper name and
  a *real* proof attempt (a partial proof beats a documented gap), as
  project-local infrastructure others can reuse.
- **Factor hard steps into their own named, reusable lemmas** rather than a
  monolithic proof — mirroring the blueprint's "split, don't abbreviate" rule.
- **Record it** so it isn't an invisible dependency: give the new declaration a
  blueprint node (`\lean{…}` + `\uses{…}`) and note it for the roadmap, so future
  sessions and the DAG can see the new frontier ([[blueprint-conventions]], [[hgraph]]).

## House style (light touch)

- Module docstring at the top; group related material into `section`s /
  `namespace`s; keep lines readable (~100 cols); align `calc` steps.
- Prefer `simp`/`grind`-normal statements so lemmas fire as `@[simp]` candidates
  and rewrites compose.
- Comments explain the *mathematics*, not the development history ("was a sorry",
  "TODO next session" — keep that in the report/inbox, not the source).
- Mark reusable facts `@[simp]` only when they're genuinely confluent rewrites.

## Faithfulness (non-negotiable)

- **Never weaken a statement to make it pass**, and never change a declaration's
  statement to dodge its proof. A proof that games the checker is a failure.
- **No `axiom` / `admit` / `native_decide` on a goal you haven't honestly
  closed**, and no `sorry` reported as done — see [[lean-check]] for verifying a
  build is genuinely sorry-free.

   102	  -- (adapter) The augmentation node `GV(Ψ F)` is the section group `Γ(V, F)`: definitional,
   103	  -- since `restrictScalars (𝟙 ·)` and `toPresheaf` leave the underlying abelian-group presheaf
   104	  -- unchanged and evaluation extracts the section over `V`.
   105	  let eY : GV.obj ((SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf ⋙
   106	        PresheafOfModules.restrictScalars α).obj F) ≅
   107	      ((SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf).obj F).presheaf.obj (Opposite.op V) := Iso.refl _
   108	  -- (compat) The evaluated Čech augmentation equals the canonical `sectionCechAugV` read through
   109	  -- `coreIso_objIso 0`; definitional, since `sectionCechAugV` is by construction
   110	  -- `GV(Ψ(cechAugmentation)) ≫ (coreIso_objIso 𝒰 F 0 V).hom` and `eY.hom = 𝟙`.
   111	  have hcompat : GV.map ((SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf ⋙
   112	        PresheafOfModules.restrictScalars α).map (cechAugmentation 𝒰 F)) ≫
   113	        (HomologicalComplex.Hom.isoApp coreIso 0).hom = eY.hom ≫ sectionCechAugV 𝒰 F V := by
   114	    have happ : (HomologicalComplex.Hom.isoApp coreIso 0).hom = (coreIso_objIso 𝒰 F 0 V).hom :=
   115	      congrArg Iso.hom (HomologicalComplex.Hom.isoOfComponents_app _ _ 0)
   116	    rw [happ, sectionCechAugV]
   117	    exact (Category.id_comp _).symm
   118	  -- Peel the augmentation node off `D` with `mapHC_augment_iso` (twice), then glue the
   119	  -- non-augmented `coreIso` to the augmentation data with `augmentCochainIso`.
   120	  exact (GV.mapHomologicalComplex cc).mapIso
   121	      (mapHC_augment_iso (SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf ⋙
   122	          PresheafOfModules.restrictScalars α) hΨadd (cechComplexOnX 𝒰 F) (cechAugmentation 𝒰 F)
   123	        (cechAugmentation_comp_d 𝒰 F)) ≪≫
   124	    mapHC_augment_iso GV ‹GV.Additive› (((SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf ⋙
   125	        PresheafOfModules.restrictScalars α).mapHomologicalComplex cc).obj (cechComplexOnX 𝒰 F))
   126	      ((SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf ⋙
   127	        PresheafOfModules.restrictScalars α).map (cechAugmentation 𝒰 F))
   128	      (map_augment_cond (SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf ⋙
   129	        PresheafOfModules.restrictScalars α) hΨadd (cechComplexOnX 𝒰 F) (cechAugmentation 𝒰 F)
   130	        (cechAugmentation_comp_d 𝒰 F)) ≪≫
   131	    augmentCochainIso coreIso eY (GV.map ((SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf ⋙
   132	        PresheafOfModules.restrictScalars α).map (cechAugmentation 𝒰 F)))
   133	      (map_augment_cond GV ‹GV.Additive› (((SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf ⋙
   134	          PresheafOfModules.restrictScalars α).mapHomologicalComplex cc).obj (cechComplexOnX 𝒰 F))
   135	        ((SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf ⋙
   136	          PresheafOfModules.restrictScalars α).map (cechAugmentation 𝒰 F))
   137	        (map_augment_cond (SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf ⋙
   138	          PresheafOfModules.restrictScalars α) hΨadd (cechComplexOnX 𝒰 F) (cechAugmentation 𝒰 F)
   139	          (cechAugmentation_comp_d 𝒰 F))) (sectionCechAugV 𝒰 F V)
   140	      (sectionCechAugV_comp_d 𝒰 F V) hcompat

    30	/-- The bottom differential of the augmented section Cech complex is its augmentation map. -/

    35	/-- The degree-zero product coordinate, kept opaque so composition can be transported without
    36	unfolding the full dependent product equivalence. -/

    38	    (t : ToType ((cechSectionAugComplex 𝒰 F V).X 1)) : cechSectionCoeff 𝒰 F V 1 σ :=
    39	  sectionCechProductEquiv (fun a => coverOpen 𝒰 a ⊓ V)
    40	    ((SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf).obj F) 0 t σ

    42	/-- The opaque degree-zero coordinate agrees with the section product equivalence. -/
    43	lemma cechSectionZeroCoord_eq (σ : Fin 1 → 𝒰.I₀)
    44	    (t : ToType ((cechSectionAugComplex 𝒰 F V).X 1)) :
    45	    cechSectionZeroCoord 𝒰 F V σ t =
    46	      sectionCechProductEquiv (fun a => coverOpen 𝒰 a ⊓ V)
    47	        ((SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf).obj F) 0 t σ :=
    48	  rfl

    54	    (cechSectionHomotopyZero 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV).hom)

   106	lemma cechSectionDepDiff_depHomotopy_zero

   119	    have hρ : ρ = Fin.elim0 := Subsingleton.elim _ _

   128	/-- The augmentation coordinate of the bottom homotopy followed by the differential is the
   129	corresponding coface restriction. -/
   130	lemma cechSectionHomotopyZero_comp_d_restriction_coord
   131	    (t : ToType ((cechSectionAugComplex 𝒰 F V).X 1)) (σ : Fin 1 → 𝒰.I₀) :
   132	    cechSectionZeroCoord 𝒰 F V σ
   133	        (ConcreteCategory.hom (cechSectionHomotopyZeroAug 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV) t)
   134	      = cechSectionCoface 𝒰 F V 0 σ 0

   137	    (cechSectionHomotopyZeroAug_apply 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV t)) ?_
   138	  exact sectionCechAugV_coord 𝒰 F V
   139	    (ConcreteCategory.hom (cechSectionHomotopyZero 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV) t) σ

   141	/-- The coordinate of the augmentation projection followed by the Cech differential is the
   142	bottom-level dependent differential of the prepended tuple. -/
   143	lemma cechSectionHomotopyZero_comp_d_coord
   144	    (t : ToType ((cechSectionAugComplex 𝒰 F V).X 1)) (σ : Fin 1 → 𝒰.I₀) :
   145	    sectionCechProductEquiv (fun a => coverOpen 𝒰 a ⊓ V)

   147	        (ConcreteCategory.hom (cechSectionHomotopyZero 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV ≫
   148	          (cechSectionAugComplex 𝒰 F V).d 0 1) t) σ

   151	            (fun τ => sectionCechProductEquiv (fun a => coverOpen 𝒰 a ⊓ V)
   152	              ((SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf).obj F) 0 t τ)) σ := by
   153	  refine Eq.trans (cechSectionZeroCoord_eq 𝒰 F V σ _).symm ?_
   154	  refine Eq.trans (congrArg (fun d => cechSectionZeroCoord 𝒰 F V σ
   155	      (ConcreteCategory.hom (cechSectionHomotopyZero 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV ≫ d) t))

   187	/-- **(I1)** The augmentation-node contracting identity:
   188	`𝟙 = π_{i_fix} ≫ ε + d⁰ ≫ h₁` on `Č⁰`. -/
   189	lemma cechSection_comm_one :
   190	    𝟙 ((cechSectionAugComplex 𝒰 F V).X 1) =
   191	      cechSectionHomotopyZero 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV ≫ (cechSectionAugComplex 𝒰 F V).d 0 1 +
   192	        (cechSectionAugComplex 𝒰 F V).d 1 2 ≫ cechSectionHomotopyComp 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV 0 := by
   193	  let E := sectionCechProductAddEquiv (fun a => coverOpen 𝒰 a ⊓ V)
   194	    ((SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf).obj F) 0
   195	  ext t
   196	  apply E.injective
   197	  funext σ
   198	  refine Eq.symm ?_
   199	  have hsplit : ConcreteCategory.hom
   200	      (cechSectionHomotopyZero 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV ≫ (cechSectionAugComplex 𝒰 F V).d 0 1 +
   201	        (cechSectionAugComplex 𝒰 F V).d 1 2 ≫ cechSectionHomotopyComp 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV 0) t
   202	      = ConcreteCategory.hom (cechSectionHomotopyZero 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV ≫
   203	          (cechSectionAugComplex 𝒰 F V).d 0 1) t +
   204	        ConcreteCategory.hom ((cechSectionAugComplex 𝒰 F V).d 1 2 ≫
   205	          cechSectionHomotopyComp 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV 0) t := by
   206	    rw [AddCommGrpCat.hom_add_apply]
   207	  refine Eq.trans (congrArg (fun y => E y σ) hsplit) ?_
   208	  refine Eq.trans (congrArg (fun y => y σ) (map_add E _ _)) ?_
   209	  refine Eq.trans (congrArg₂ (· + ·)
   210	    (cechSectionHomotopyZero_comp_d_coord 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV t σ)
   211	    (cechSectionD_comp_homotopyComp_zero_coord 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV t σ)) ?_
   212	  refine Eq.trans (CombinatorialCech.depHomotopy_spec i_fix (cechSectionCoface 𝒰 F V)
   213	    (cechSectionPrepend 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV)
   214	    (fun {m} σ' y => cechSection_hu 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV σ' y)
   215	    (fun {m} σ' k y => cechSection_hsh 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV σ' k y)

   217	      ((SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf).obj F) 0 t τ) σ) ?_
   218	  exact congrArg (fun y => E y σ) (ConcreteCategory.id_apply t).symm

   407	/-- **Coordinatewise identification of the canonical augmentation** (the degree-`0`
   408	augmentation seam of `lem:cechSection_contractible`): the `σ`-coordinate of
   409	`sectionCechAugV` is the plain restriction `Γ(V, F) → Γ(U'_σ, F)`.  This is the `p = 0`
   410	leg unwinding of `coreIso_objIso` — through `pushPull_sigma_iso`'s `σ`-leg, the terminal
   411	object of `Over X` (which collapses `a₀(σ) ≫ (augmentation)` to the canonical map
   412	`Over.mk j_σ ⟶ Over.mk (𝟙 X)` with NO unwinding of `a₀`), and the section computation of
   413	the push–pull adjunction unit. -/
   414	lemma sectionCechAugV_π (𝒰 : X.OpenCover) [Finite 𝒰.I₀] (F : X.Modules)
   415	    (V : TopologicalSpace.Opens X) (σ : Fin 1 → 𝒰.I₀) :
   416	    sectionCechAugV 𝒰 F V ≫ Pi.π (fun τ : Fin 1 → 𝒰.I₀ =>
   417	        ((SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf).obj F).presheaf.obj
   418	          (Opposite.op (⨅ l, (coverOpen 𝒰 (τ l) ⊓ V)))) σ =
   419	      ((SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf).obj F).presheaf.map
   420	        (homOfLE (restrictedIntersection_le 𝒰 V σ)).op := by
   421	  have hproj := coreIso_objIso_π 𝒰 F 0 V σ
   422	  have hGE := GVΨ_map_eq V (cechAugmentation 𝒰 F)
   423	  -- The augmentation collapses through the terminal object to the
   424	  -- adjunction unit, which reads as the plain restriction; the residual transports are
   425	  -- parallel restriction chains between the same opens.
   426	  refine Eq.trans (congrArg (fun m => m ≫ _) (rfl :
   427	    sectionCechAugV 𝒰 F V =
   428	      (PresheafOfModules.toPresheaf X.ringCatSheaf.obj ⋙
   429	          (evaluation (TopologicalSpace.Opens ↥X)ᵒᵖ AddCommGrpCat).obj (Opposite.op V)).map
   430	        ((SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf ⋙
   431	          PresheafOfModules.restrictScalars (𝟙 X.ringCatSheaf.obj)).map
   432	            (cechAugmentation 𝒰 F)) ≫
   433	        (coreIso_objIso 𝒰 F 0 V).hom)) ?_
   434	  refine Eq.trans (Category.assoc _ _ _) ?_
   435	  refine Eq.trans (congrArg (fun m => _ ≫ m) hproj) ?_
   436	  refine Eq.trans (Category.assoc _ _ _).symm ?_
   437	  refine Eq.trans (congrArg (fun m => m ≫ ((pushPull_leg_sections 𝒰 F σ V).hom ≫
   438	      eqToHom (congrArg
   439	        (fun W => ((SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf).obj F).presheaf.obj

     6	import Mathlib
     7	
     8	/-!
     9	# Degree-one Čech cobounding for the structure sheaf on an affine open
    10	
    11	This file proves the algebraic core of degree-one cohomology vanishing on affine opens
    12	(Serre): on an affine open `U` of a scheme `X`, every Čech 1-cocycle for the structure
    13	sheaf on a finite cover of `U` by basic opens is a coboundary
    14	(`AlgebraicGeometry.IsAffineOpen.exists_cech_cobounding`).
    15	
    16	The proof is the classical partition-of-unity argument, carried out entirely in the
    17	language of sections of the structure sheaf (no abstract localizations appear in the
    18	statement): given a cocycle `a i j ∈ Γ(X, D(f i) ⊓ D(f j))` for `f : Fin n → Γ(X, U)`
    19	with `⨆ i, D(f i) = U`,
    20	
    21	1. *clear denominators* (`IsAffineOpen.exists_res_eq_pow_mul`): each `f j ^ N * a i j`
    22	   extends to a section `e i j` on `D(f i)`, with one uniform exponent `N`;
    23	2. *annihilate the defects* (`IsAffineOpen.exists_pow_mul_eq_zero_of_res_eq_zero`): the
    24	   defect `t i j l = e i l - e j l - f l ^ N * a i j` on `D(f i) ⊓ D(f j)` restricts to
    25	   zero on the triple intersection by the cocycle identity, so `f l ^ M * t i j l = 0`
    26	   for one uniform `M`;
    27	3. *partition of unity*: `1 = ∑ h l * f l ^ (N + M)` in `Γ(X, U)` since the `D(f i)`
    28	   cover `U`, and `b i = ∑ l, h l * (f l ^ M * e i l)` is the desired cobounding.
    29	
    30	Both helper lemmas are the `IsLocalization.Away` property of sections over basic opens of
    31	an affine open, repackaged through `Scheme.resHom`; they are stated for a section `g`
    32	living on any open `W ≥ U`, which is the form needed in the main argument (there `U` is a
    33	basic open of the cover and `W` the ambient affine open).
    34	
    35	The statements are for an arbitrary scheme `X` and an affine open `U`; the affine-scheme
    36	case is `U = ⊤`. This file is `Ext`-free; it is consumed by
    37	`AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.AffineVanishing`.
    38	-/
    39	
    40	set_option autoImplicit false
    41	
    42	universe u
    43	
    44	open CategoryTheory Opposite TopologicalSpace
    45	
    46	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    47	
    48	namespace Scheme
    49	
    50	variable (X : Scheme.{u})
    51	
    52	/-- Restriction of sections of the structure sheaf along an inclusion of opens, as a ring
    53	homomorphism. A convenience wrapper around `X.presheaf.map` that composes cleanly
    54	(`Scheme.resHom_resHom`); the inclusion proof argument is proof-irrelevant. -/
    55	noncomputable def resHom {U V : X.Opens} (h : V ≤ U) : Γ(X, U) →+* Γ(X, V) :=
    56	  (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE h).op).hom
    57	
    58	variable {X}
    59	
    60	@[simp]
    61	lemma resHom_resHom {U V W : X.Opens} (h₁ : V ≤ U) (h₂ : W ≤ V) (t : Γ(X, U)) :
    62	    X.resHom h₂ (X.resHom h₁ t) = X.resHom (h₂.trans h₁) t := by
    63	  rw [resHom, resHom, resHom, ← CommRingCat.comp_apply, ← X.presheaf.map_comp,
    64	    ← op_comp, homOfLE_comp]
    65	
    66	lemma resHom_refl {U : X.Opens} (t : Γ(X, U)) : X.resHom le_rfl t = t := by
    67	  have h : (homOfLE (le_refl U)).op = 𝟙 (op U) := rfl
    68	  rw [resHom, h, X.presheaf.map_id]
    69	  rfl
    70	
    71	/-- Restriction along `U ≤ U` is the identity (for an arbitrary proof, which is
    72	proof-irrelevant). -/
    73	@[simp]
    74	lemma resHom_self {U : X.Opens} (h : U ≤ U) (t : Γ(X, U)) : X.resHom h t = t :=
    75	  resHom_refl t
    76	
    77	lemma basicOpen_resHom {U W : X.Opens} (h : U ≤ W) (g : Γ(X, W)) :
    78	    X.basicOpen (X.resHom h g) = U ⊓ X.basicOpen g :=
    79	  X.basicOpen_res _ _
    80	
    81	/-- The canonical algebra structure on sections over a basic open (mathlib's
    82	`algebra_section_section_basicOpen` instance), in `resHom` normal form. -/
    83	lemma algebraMap_basicOpen_eq_resHom {U : X.Opens} (f : Γ(X, U)) :
    84	    algebraMap Γ(X, U) Γ(X, X.basicOpen f) = X.resHom (X.basicOpen_le f) :=
    85	  rfl
    86	
    87	end Scheme
    88	
    89	namespace IsAffineOpen
    90	
    91	open Scheme
    92	
    93	variable {X : Scheme.{u}} {U W : X.Opens} (hU : IsAffineOpen U) (hUW : U ≤ W)
    94	  (g : Γ(X, W))
    95	
    96	include hU in
    97	/-- Denominator clearing on an affine open: a section `c` of the structure sheaf on
    98	`U ⊓ D(g)` becomes the restriction of a section on `U` after multiplication by a power
    99	of `g` (a section on any open `W ≥ U`). -/
   100	theorem exists_res_eq_pow_mul (c : Γ(X, U ⊓ X.basicOpen g)) :
   101	    ∃ (N : ℕ) (e : Γ(X, U)),
   102	      X.resHom inf_le_left e = X.resHom (inf_le_left.trans hUW) g ^ N * c := by
   103	  have hb : X.basicOpen (X.resHom hUW g) = U ⊓ X.basicOpen g :=
   104	    basicOpen_resHom hUW g
   105	  haveI := hU.isLocalization_basicOpen (X.resHom hUW g)
   106	  obtain ⟨⟨y, m⟩, hy⟩ := IsLocalization.surj
   107	    (M := Submonoid.powers (X.resHom hUW g)) (X.resHom hb.le c)
   108	  dsimp only at hy
   109	  obtain ⟨Nm, hNm⟩ := (Submonoid.mem_powers_iff (m : Γ(X, U))
   110	    (X.resHom hUW g)).mp m.2
   111	  refine ⟨Nm, y, ?_⟩
   112	  have hy' := congrArg (X.resHom hb.ge) hy
   113	  rw [← hNm] at hy'
   114	  simp only [Scheme.algebraMap_basicOpen_eq_resHom, map_mul, map_pow, resHom_resHom,
   115	    resHom_self] at hy'
   116	  linear_combination -hy'
   117	
   118	include hU in
   119	/-- Annihilation on an affine open: a section of the structure sheaf on `U` restricting to
   120	zero on `U ⊓ D(g)` is killed by a power of `g`. -/
   121	theorem exists_pow_mul_eq_zero_of_res_eq_zero (t : Γ(X, U))
   122	    (ht : X.resHom (inf_le_left : U ⊓ X.basicOpen g ≤ U) t = 0) :
   123	    ∃ M : ℕ, X.resHom hUW g ^ M * t = 0 := by
   124	  have hb : X.basicOpen (X.resHom hUW g) = U ⊓ X.basicOpen g :=
   125	    basicOpen_resHom hUW g
   126	  haveI := hU.isLocalization_basicOpen (X.resHom hUW g)
   127	  have h0 : algebraMap Γ(X, U) Γ(X, X.basicOpen (X.resHom hUW g)) t = 0 := by
   128	    rw [Scheme.algebraMap_basicOpen_eq_resHom]
   129	    have hcomp : X.resHom (X.basicOpen_le (X.resHom hUW g)) t =
   130	        X.resHom hb.le (X.resHom inf_le_left t) := by
   131	      rw [Scheme.resHom_resHom]
   132	    rw [hcomp, ht, map_zero]
   133	  obtain ⟨m, hm⟩ := (IsLocalization.map_eq_zero_iff
   134	    (Submonoid.powers (X.resHom hUW g)) _ t).mp h0
   135	  obtain ⟨M, hM⟩ := (Submonoid.mem_powers_iff (m : Γ(X, U))
   136	    (X.resHom hUW g)).mp m.2
   137	  refine ⟨M, ?_⟩
   138	  calc X.resHom hUW g ^ M * t = ↑m * t := by rw [← hM]
   139	    _ = 0 := hm

     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.CechSectionIdentification
     7	
     8	/-!
     9	# Components of the concrete section Čech contraction
    10	
    11	This file constructs the restriction maps and homotopy components for the augmented concrete
    12	section Čech complex, together with the degree-zero contracting identity.
    13	-/
    14	
    15	universe u
    16	
    17	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite
    18	
    19	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    20	
    21	open Scheme.Modules
    22	
    23	variable {X : Scheme.{u}}
    24	
    25	/-! ### Additive product coordinates -/
    26	
    27	/-- The additive form of the dependent product coordinates used by the concrete section Čech
    28	complex.  Keeping the product equivalence bundled avoids repeating its additivity proof at each
    29	coordinatewise contracting identity. -/
    30	noncomputable def sectionCechProductAddEquiv {ι : Type u}
    31	    (U : ι → TopologicalSpace.Opens X) (F : X.PresheafOfModules) (p : ℕ) :
    32	    ToType ((sectionCechCosimplicial U F).obj (SimplexCategory.mk p)) ≃+
    33	      (∀ σ : Fin (p + 1) → ι,
    34	        ToType (F.presheaf.obj (Opposite.op (⨅ k, U (σ k))))) where
    35	  toFun := sectionCechProductEquiv U F p
    36	  invFun := (sectionCechProductEquiv U F p).symm
    37	  left_inv := (sectionCechProductEquiv U F p).left_inv
    38	  right_inv := (sectionCechProductEquiv U F p).right_inv
    39	  map_add' x y := by
    40	    funext σ
    41	    simp only [sectionCechProductEquiv_apply, Pi.add_apply]
    42	    exact map_add _ x y
    43	
    44	/-! ## Contracting homotopy on the augmented concrete section Čech complex -/
    45	
    46	/-! ### Restriction engine
    47	
    48	The dependent-coefficient combinatorial Čech engine (`CombinatorialCech.depHomotopy_spec`,
    49	CechAcyclic.lean) is instantiated with the augmentation node `Γ(V, F)` as level `0` and the
    50	restricted Čech coefficients `Γ(⨅ₖ (U_{σ k} ⊓ V), F)` as levels `≥ 1`.  The coface maps `δ`
    51	are the presheaf face restrictions (level `0 → 1` is the augmentation restriction), and the
    52	prepend maps `c` are genuine restrictions because `V ≤ coverOpen 𝒰 i_fix` forces
    53	`U'_{i_fix·σ} = U'_σ`.  The `hu`/`hsh` compatibilities collapse to "two parallel restriction
    54	chains between the same opens agree". -/
    55	
    56	section RestrictionEngine
    57	
    58	variable (𝒰 : X.OpenCover) (F : X.Modules) (V : TopologicalSpace.Opens X)
    59	
    60	/-- Composite of two presheaf restrictions is the direct restriction (local copy of the
    61	`CechBridge` private helper `restr_trans`). -/
    62	private lemma restriction_comp_apply (P : (TopologicalSpace.Opens ↥X)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Ab.{u})
    63	    {A B C : TopologicalSpace.Opens ↥X} (h1 : A ≤ B) (h2 : B ≤ C)
    64	    (x : ToType (P.obj (Opposite.op C))) :
    65	    ConcreteCategory.hom (P.map (homOfLE h1).op)
    66	        (ConcreteCategory.hom (P.map (homOfLE h2).op) x)
    67	      = ConcreteCategory.hom (P.map (homOfLE (h1.trans h2)).op) x := by
    68	  rw [← ConcreteCategory.comp_apply, ← P.map_comp, ← op_comp]
    69	  rfl
    70	
    71	/-- Two parallel presheaf restrictions agree (poset-hom uniqueness; local copy of the
    72	`CechBridge` private helper `restr_op_unique`). -/
    73	private lemma restriction_eq_of_parallel (P : (TopologicalSpace.Opens ↥X)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Ab.{u})
    74	    {A C : TopologicalSpace.Opens ↥X} (f g : Opposite.op C ⟶ Opposite.op A)
    75	    (x : ToType (P.obj (Opposite.op C))) :
    76	    ConcreteCategory.hom (P.map f) x = ConcreteCategory.hom (P.map g) x := by
    77	  rw [show f = g from Quiver.Hom.unop_inj (Subsingleton.elim _ _)]
    78	
    79	/-- A nonempty restricted Čech intersection is contained in `V`. -/
    80	private lemma restrictedIntersection_le {m : ℕ} (σ : Fin (m + 1) → 𝒰.I₀) :
    81	    (⨅ k, (coverOpen 𝒰 (σ k) ⊓ V)) ≤ V :=
    82	  le_trans (iInf_le _ 0) inf_le_right
    83	
    84	/-- Prepending `i_fix` does not shrink the restricted intersection (positive levels). -/
    85	private lemma restrictedIntersection_le_cons {m : ℕ} (i_fix : 𝒰.I₀) (hiV : V ≤ coverOpen 𝒰 i_fix)
    86	    (σ : Fin (m + 1) → 𝒰.I₀) :
    87	    (⨅ k, (coverOpen 𝒰 (σ k) ⊓ V)) ≤
    88	      ⨅ k, (coverOpen 𝒰 ((Fin.cons i_fix σ : Fin (m + 2) → 𝒰.I₀) k) ⊓ V) := by
    89	  refine le_iInf fun k => ?_
    90	  refine Fin.cases ?_ ?_ k
    91	  · rw [Fin.cons_zero]
    92	    exact le_trans (restrictedIntersection_le 𝒰 V σ) (le_inf hiV le_rfl)
    93	  · intro j
    94	    rw [Fin.cons_succ]
    95	    exact iInf_le _ j
    96	
    97	/-- Prepending `i_fix` to the empty tuple yields an intersection containing `V`
    98	(the augmentation node case). -/
    99	private lemma le_restrictedIntersection_cons_empty (i_fix : 𝒰.I₀) (hiV : V ≤ coverOpen 𝒰 i_fix)
   100	    (σ : Fin 0 → 𝒰.I₀) :
   101	    V ≤ ⨅ k, (coverOpen 𝒰 ((Fin.cons i_fix σ : Fin 1 → 𝒰.I₀) k) ⊓ V) := by
   102	  refine le_iInf fun k => ?_
   103	  rw [Fin.fin_one_eq_zero k, Fin.cons_zero]
   104	  exact le_inf hiV le_rfl
   105	
   106	/-- The open underlying the level-`m` contracting-homotopy coefficient: level `0` is `V` (the
   107	augmentation node), level `m+1` is the restricted intersection `⨅ₖ (U_{σ k} ⊓ V)`. -/
   108	private def homotopyOpen : (m : ℕ) → (Fin m → 𝒰.I₀) → TopologicalSpace.Opens ↥X
   109	  | 0, _ => V
   110	  | _ + 1, σ => ⨅ k, (coverOpen 𝒰 (σ k) ⊓ V)
   111	
   112	/-- The coface inclusion of the contracting-homotopy opens. -/
   113	private lemma homotopyOpen_le_coface : ∀ {m : ℕ} (σ : Fin (m + 1) → 𝒰.I₀) (j : Fin (m + 1)),
   114	    homotopyOpen 𝒰 V (m + 1) σ ≤ homotopyOpen 𝒰 V m (σ ∘ j.succAbove)
   115	  | 0, σ, _ => restrictedIntersection_le 𝒰 V σ
   116	  | _ + 1, _, j => le_iInf fun l => iInf_le _ (j.succAbove l)
   117	
   118	/-- The prepend inclusion of the contracting-homotopy opens (prepending `i_fix` does not shrink the
   119	open, because `V ≤ coverOpen 𝒰 i_fix`). -/
   120	private lemma homotopyOpen_le_prepend (i_fix : 𝒰.I₀) (hiV : V ≤ coverOpen 𝒰 i_fix) :
   121	    ∀ {m : ℕ} (σ : Fin m → 𝒰.I₀),
   122	      homotopyOpen 𝒰 V m σ ≤ homotopyOpen 𝒰 V (m + 1) (Fin.cons i_fix σ)
   123	  | 0, σ => le_restrictedIntersection_cons_empty 𝒰 V i_fix hiV σ
   124	  | _ + 1, σ => restrictedIntersection_le_cons 𝒰 V i_fix hiV σ
   125	
   126	/-- Dependent coefficient family for the contracting-homotopy engine: the sections of `F` over
   127	`homotopyOpen m σ`.  Kept as a reducible abbreviation so the `AddCommGroup` instance is the
   128	generic one on `Ab`-objects (no bespoke match-instance). -/
   129	noncomputable abbrev cechSectionCoeff (m : ℕ) (σ : Fin m → 𝒰.I₀) : Type u :=
   130	  ToType (((SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf).obj F).presheaf.obj
   131	    (Opposite.op (homotopyOpen 𝒰 V m σ)))
   132	
   133	/-- The engine coface maps: presheaf face restrictions (level `0 → 1` is the augmentation
   134	restriction `Γ(V) → Γ(U'_σ)`). -/
   135	noncomputable def cechSectionCoface (m : ℕ) (σ : Fin (m + 1) → 𝒰.I₀)
   136	    (j : Fin (m + 1)) :
   137	    cechSectionCoeff 𝒰 F V m (σ ∘ j.succAbove) →+ cechSectionCoeff 𝒰 F V (m + 1) σ :=
   138	  ConcreteCategory.hom (((SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf).obj F).presheaf.map
   139	    (homOfLE (homotopyOpen_le_coface 𝒰 V σ j)).op)
   140	
   141	/-- The engine prepend maps: genuine restrictions (level `1 → 0` is the restriction
   142	`Γ(U'_{(i_fix)}) → Γ(V)` along `V ≤ U'_{i_fix}`). -/
   143	noncomputable def cechSectionPrepend (i_fix : 𝒰.I₀)
   144	    (hiV : V ≤ coverOpen 𝒰 i_fix) (m : ℕ) (σ : Fin m → 𝒰.I₀) :
   145	    cechSectionCoeff 𝒰 F V (m + 1) (Fin.cons i_fix σ) →+ cechSectionCoeff 𝒰 F V m σ :=
   146	  ConcreteCategory.hom (((SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf).obj F).presheaf.map
   147	    (homOfLE (homotopyOpen_le_prepend 𝒰 V i_fix hiV σ)).op)
   148	
   149	/-- Transport of a Čech coefficient along an equality of index tuples is the canonical
   150	restriction between the (equal) intersection opens. -/
   151	private lemma cechSectionCoeff_transport {m : ℕ} {τ₁ τ₂ : Fin (m + 1) → 𝒰.I₀}
   152	    (h : τ₁ = τ₂)
   153	    (hle : homotopyOpen 𝒰 V (m + 1) τ₂ ≤ homotopyOpen 𝒰 V (m + 1) τ₁)
   154	    (y : cechSectionCoeff 𝒰 F V (m + 1) τ₁) :
   155	    (h ▸ y : cechSectionCoeff 𝒰 F V (m + 1) τ₂)
   156	      = ConcreteCategory.hom
   157	          (((SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf).obj F).presheaf.map (homOfLE hle).op)
   158	          y := by
   159	  subst h
   160	  rw [show homOfLE hle = 𝟙 _ from Subsingleton.elim _ _, op_id,
   161	    CategoryTheory.Functor.map_id]
   162	  rfl
   163	
   164	/-- Unit compatibility `hu` for the contracting-homotopy engine: deleting the prepended
   165	`i_fix` and then applying the prepend restriction is the identity transport (both sides are
   166	restriction chains between the same opens). -/
   167	lemma cechSection_hu (i_fix : 𝒰.I₀) (hiV : V ≤ coverOpen 𝒰 i_fix)
   168	    {m : ℕ} (σ : Fin (m + 1) → 𝒰.I₀)
   169	    (y : cechSectionCoeff 𝒰 F V (m + 1)
   170	      ((Fin.cons i_fix σ : Fin (m + 2) → 𝒰.I₀) ∘ (0 : Fin (m + 2)).succAbove)) :
   171	    cechSectionPrepend 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV (m + 1) σ
   172	        (cechSectionCoface 𝒰 F V (m + 1) (Fin.cons i_fix σ) 0 y)
   173	      = (CombinatorialCech.cons_comp_zero_succAbove i_fix σ) ▸ y := by
   174	  rw [cechSectionCoeff_transport 𝒰 F V (CombinatorialCech.cons_comp_zero_succAbove i_fix σ)
   175	    (le_of_eq (by rw [CombinatorialCech.cons_comp_zero_succAbove i_fix σ]))]
   176	  exact (restriction_comp_apply _ _ _ y).trans (restriction_eq_of_parallel _ _ _ y)
   177	
   178	/-- Shift compatibility `hsh` for the contracting-homotopy engine: prepend commutes with the later
   179	cofaces (both sides are restriction chains between the same opens). -/
   180	lemma cechSection_hsh (i_fix : 𝒰.I₀) (hiV : V ≤ coverOpen 𝒰 i_fix)
   181	    {m : ℕ} (σ : Fin (m + 1) → 𝒰.I₀) (k : Fin (m + 1))
   182	    (y : cechSectionCoeff 𝒰 F V (m + 1)
   183	      ((Fin.cons i_fix σ : Fin (m + 2) → 𝒰.I₀) ∘ (k.succ).succAbove)) :
   184	    cechSectionPrepend 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV (m + 1) σ
   185	        (cechSectionCoface 𝒰 F V (m + 1) (Fin.cons i_fix σ) k.succ y)
   186	      = cechSectionCoface 𝒰 F V m σ k
   187	          (cechSectionPrepend 𝒰 F V i_fix hiV m (σ ∘ k.succAbove)
   188	            ((CombinatorialCech.cons_comp_succAbove_succ i_fix σ k) ▸ y)) := by
   189	  have hle : homotopyOpen 𝒰 V (m + 1) (Fin.cons i_fix (σ ∘ k.succAbove)) ≤
   190	      homotopyOpen 𝒰 V (m + 1) ((Fin.cons i_fix σ : Fin (m + 2) → 𝒰.I₀) ∘ (k.succ).succAbove) :=
   191	    le_of_eq (by rw [CombinatorialCech.cons_comp_succAbove_succ i_fix σ k])
   192	  rw [cechSectionCoeff_transport 𝒰 F V
   193	    (CombinatorialCech.cons_comp_succAbove_succ i_fix σ k) hle]
   194	  refine Eq.trans (restriction_comp_apply _ (homotopyOpen_le_prepend 𝒰 V i_fix hiV σ)
   195	    (homotopyOpen_le_coface 𝒰 V (Fin.cons i_fix σ) k.succ) y) ?_
   196	  refine Eq.trans (restriction_eq_of_parallel _ _ (homOfLE ((homotopyOpen_le_coface 𝒰 V σ k).trans
   197	    ((homotopyOpen_le_prepend 𝒰 V i_fix hiV (σ ∘ k.succAbove)).trans hle))).op y) ?_
   198	  refine Eq.symm ?_
   199	  refine Eq.trans (DFunLike.congr_arg (cechSectionCoface 𝒰 F V m σ k)
   200	    (restriction_comp_apply _ (homotopyOpen_le_prepend 𝒰 V i_fix hiV (σ ∘ k.succAbove)) hle y)) ?_
   201	  exact restriction_comp_apply _ (homotopyOpen_le_coface 𝒰 V σ k)
   202	    ((homotopyOpen_le_prepend 𝒰 V i_fix hiV (σ ∘ k.succAbove)).trans hle) y
   203	
   204	end RestrictionEngine

1. Add a lightweight `CechSectionComplex` module containing the generic direct augmentation and its cancellation proof.
2. Rewire `sectionCechAugV` to that definition, move the transported comparison into `CechSectionIdentification`, and remove identification machinery from the contraction core.

/-!
# Sub-brick A: identifying the evaluated augmented Čech section complex
  (blueprint `lem:cech_backbone_left_sigma` … `lem:cechSection_contractible`)

This file is the shared "Sub-brick A" chain that

1. identifies the degree-`p` Čech-nerve backbone `(coverCechNerveOver 𝒰).obj [p]` with
   the coproduct `∐_σ Over.mk j_σ` in `Over X` (`cechBackbone_left_sigma`);
2. decomposes the push-pull object `pushPullObj F Y_p` as a product in `X.Modules`
   (`pushPull_sigma_iso`) — the single new-infra leaf;
3. identifies the sections of each leg over an open `V` with `Γ(U_σ ∩ V, F)`
   (`pushPull_leg_sections`);
4. assembles the degreewise section isomorphism `Γ(V, pushPullObj F Y_p) ≅ ∏_σ Γ(U_σ ∩ V, F)`
   (`pushPull_eval_prod_iso`);
5. promotes these degreewise isos to a complex isomorphism
